title: India's 15-Month Inflation Streak Is Over. Economists Say Prices Just Hit the RBI's Red Line.
excerpt: A Reuters poll of 38 economists forecasts India's CPI inflation at 4% in May — breaching the Reserve Bank's target for the first time since early 2025 — as fuel price hikes and vegetable costs tear through household budgets.
body:
For fifteen consecutive months, India managed to keep consumer inflation below the Reserve Bank of India's 4% target — a run that gave the central bank room to cut rates, kept household budgets relatively stable, and provided a rare bright spot in an economy buffeted by global headwinds. That streak is almost certainly over.

A Reuters poll of 38 economists forecasts that India's Consumer Price Index rose to 4.0% in May, up from 3.48% in April. When the official data drops later this week, it will likely confirm what grocery bills across the country have already made obvious: the Iran war is no longer an abstract geopolitical event. It is showing up in the price of cooking oil, vegetables, petrol, and the auto-rickshaw ride to work.

## Fuel Did the Damage First

State-owned fuel retailers raised petrol and diesel prices four times in May alone, passing through crude oil costs that have remained stubbornly above $90 a barrel since the conflict disrupted supply routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The pass-through was immediate and brutal: transport inflation is estimated to have jumped from minus 0.01% in April to 4.15% in May, contributing 36 basis points to headline inflation — up from nearly zero the previous month.

"Persistence of elevated temperatures across several regions and war-led constraints have adversely impacted the supply of commodities," said Kanika Pasricha, chief economic adviser at Union Bank of India. "Vegetable prices have rebounded in the ongoing summer months, coupled with the severe heatwave."

## Wholesale Prices Are Screaming Louder

While CPI is the number the RBI officially targets, the Wholesale Price Index tells a more alarming story. WPI inflation more than doubled to a 42-month high of 8.3% in April, driven by a staggering 24.71% spike in fuel and power costs — up from just 1.05% the previous month. ICRA estimates WPI could cross 9% in May if energy trends continue.

The divergence between wholesale and consumer inflation will not last. When manufacturers and distributors face input costs rising at 8%, they eventually pass those increases to consumers. The question is not whether CPI will move higher but how far above 4% it will go before the monsoon and, potentially, a ceasefire bring relief.

## What the RBI Is Thinking

The central bank held interest rates steady at its meeting last week, as expected. Governor Sanjay Malhotra acknowledged that underlying inflation pressures remained "benign" but added that "second-round effects warranted vigilance." Translation: the RBI is watching whether fuel and food price increases are starting to contaminate everything else — rent, services, wages.

Interest rate swap markets are already pricing in at least 25 basis points of rate hikes over the next three months and more than 75 basis points over the next year. If those expectations materialise, the rate-cut cycle that began in late 2025 would be decisively over, replaced by a tightening cycle that would raise borrowing costs for home loans, car loans, and business credit.

## The NRI Dimension

For the diaspora, India's inflation trajectory hits twice. First, it erodes the purchasing power of remittances. An NRI sending $1,000 home to family in Hyderabad or Lucknow is already getting fewer rupees per dollar than six months ago because of the currency's slide. Now each of those rupees buys less at the vegetable market and the petrol pump.

Second, it complicates the investment case. If the RBI is forced into rate hikes, bond prices will fall, equity markets will face another headwind, and the growth slowdown that economists like Sat Duhra of Janus Henderson have warned about becomes harder to avoid.

The RBI has projected inflation averaging 5.1% for the fiscal year ending March 2027. That assumes the Iran war does not escalate further and that the monsoon performs normally. Both assumptions are fragile. The fifteen-month streak was comfortable while it lasted. The months ahead will not be.

**Sources:** Reuters, TBS News, The Indian Eye, Reserve Bank of India
